newsitem.title: CANADA: Three of four IPL crude lines reopened after spill.
newsitem.headline: Three of four IPL crude lines reopened after spill.

text.p: IPL Energy Inc said Friday that three of four lines on its Interprovincial pipeline system which were closed after a local Manitoba resident reported an oil smell were reopened and the fourth is expected back up later in the day.
Lines one, two and 13 were back up, though line three remained closed after a small spill was reported early morning in Manitoba.
Alon Roth, spokesman for IPL, said the spill was originally estimated at 30 cubic meters which is about 180/190 barrels but this was later revised to just 10 barrels.
IPL said in its "hotline" that it expects line three to recommence throughput by midnight.

Interprovincial combines with the Lakehead system on the U.S. side of the border and the system, running from Edmonton, Alberta through Superior, Wis. and Chicago to various points in southern Ontario, is the world's longest crude oil and liquids pipeline complex.

IPL lost throughput for several days earlier this month after bad weather in Minnesota knocked out three pumping stations. The throughput prior to that incident was 1.4 million barrels and the outage cut half Canada's oil movement temporarily.
